messages:
acme-bob: Hey team — started seeing a bunch of failures from our embeddings pipeline hitting Redwood's embeddings endpoint. Error in our logs: "400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768 got 1536". This only happens when we enable client-side batching; single-item calls are fine. We use python sdk v0.9.2 and model `open-embed-small-768`. Repro below:

acme-bob: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=... )
texts = ['foo'] * 32
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='open-embed-small-768', input=texts, batch_size=32)
print([len(v) for v in resp.data])
```

acme-bob: When batched, the server returns vectors of length 1536 for some items, which breaks our downstream PCA/annoy index. Any ideas?

Maya (Support): Thanks for the repro — super helpful. Quick questions: do you ever pass mixed models or override `model` at per-item level? Are any inputs binary or base64? Also can you share the raw error payload (full response body) when it fails?

acme-bob: No mixes, all same model. Inputs are plain UTF-8 strings. Raw response snippet: `{ "error": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768 got 1536", "item_index": 7 }`

Jorge (SDK): tagging in — this looks like something we saw internally. Two likely causes: 1) client-side batching code is accidentally duplicating the request body for some inputs (so server runs a different model routing) or 2) a routed fallback to a larger variant happened when a region was overloaded. Can you `curl` the endpoint directly (no SDK) with a failing batch and return the response? That'll rule out SDK bug.

acme-bob: Did a direct curl against the hosted API and got the same mismatch. Payload: `{"input": ["foo", "foo", ... 32 items], "model":"open-embed-small-768"}`. Response still returns 1536 for indexes 6..9.

Liz (DevEx): FYI, SDKs recently changed batching defaults (we moved to an adaptive batcher in 0.9.x). There's a known issue tracked in RED-3456 where rare multibyte/emoji strings hit a path that sets `force_model_variant` and the router returns the high-dim variant (1536). Not supposed to happen for `open-embed-small-768`.

Jorge (SDK): Adding more concrete repros I found in our test matrix — if the batch contains at least one string with >1024 bytes (rare) and the request crosses a kernel boundary, router may fallback to `open-embed-large-1536` for throughput reasons. Server should normalize dimensions or error earlier; we didn't expect downstream indexers to break.

Maya (Support): Ok — plan: 1) we will add a clearer error on the server that includes `model_returned` and `expected_dim` so downstream can reject consistently; 2) temporary customer workaround: set `batch_size=1` or `max_batch_bytes` lower in SDK or disable adaptive batching; 3) SDK fix: prevent adaptive batcher from mixing inputs that could trigger variant routing.

acme-bob: Workaround is fine short-term but batch_size=1 kills throughput. Any ETA on a proper fix?

Jorge (SDK): I have a patch that pins model in the batch payload (explicit `model: open-embed-small-768` per inner request) and prevents the adaptive batcher from coalescing across requests that have different internal heuristics. We'll cut python 0.9.3 and node 1.3.5 with that change today. Go SDK also needs a tiny fix for context timeout behavior we found — default context timeout was too aggressive for larger batches and triggered retries that sometimes re-sent with different routing headers.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: rdw-embeddings-router v2.4.1 -> canary (3 nodes)

Liz (DevEx): For customers who can't change batch_size, a shorter-term client-side tweak is to add `headers={"x-redwood-prefer-variant":"small"}` on the request if using raw HTTP or set `force_variant='small'` in upcoming SDKs. We'll document it in the release notes.

Jorge (SDK): Quick note about retries/timeouts: If your integration does automatic retries on 5xx or timeouts without idempotency protection, you can end up with duplicated requests that the router treats as separate and may route differently. For Go clients: ensure you pass a context with >= 2s for a 32-item batch, or use exponential backoff with jitter. For TS/Python, increase `timeout` on the client or set `retry_policy` to avoid immediate retry on 504.

acme-bob: Tried the canary header `x-redwood-prefer-variant: small` and the failing batch is now returning consistent 768 vectors. Throughput looks good.

Maya (Support): Great — followups: we've created internal ticket RED-3456 to hard-fail batches that would return mixed dims and to add `model_returned` to error payloads. SDK releases are planned for today. We'll also add a KB article documenting recommended batch_size vs expected latency for each embed model.

Jorge (SDK): Released patches: python 0.9.3 (non-adaptive batch fallback, pin model per-subrequest), node 1.3.5 (same), go 0.2.8 (context timeout defaults increased + retry idempotency improvements). Please upgrade when convenient.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy success: rdw-embeddings-router v2.4.1 -> canary healthy (3/3)

acme-bob: Upgraded python SDK to 0.9.3 and verified: 1) batch responses all 768 dims, 2) no additional errors. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Closing loop — we'll leave RED-3456 open to track the server-side validation/clearer errors and doc KB. If you see any regressions ping us and we'll reopen.

acme-bob: Thanks all!
